title: Elgar’s march: orchestra and band
work: Pomp and Circumstance — March No. 1, Op. 39
question: How do Elgar and Stock pace the returning march and final trio, and what changes in the concert-band version?
intro: Elgar’s Queen’s Hall recording and Stock’s Chicago recording were both made in 1926 and issued by Victor in 1927, as the session sources and contemporary trade bulletins document. Stock’s label explicitly credits grand organ; the Marine Band plays an unidentified concert-band arrangement. Stock’s map covers 0:05–4:18 of both transfers, while band switching covers only the returning march and final trio, Elgar 2:08–4:18 against band 3:20–5:43, avoiding the unmatched earlier repetition. Band pitch-class features are shifted two semitones for matching, but the audio is unaltered.
